Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.﴾

Tafsir of Surat al-Mulk (The Dominion)

It is a Meccan surah.

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a surah of the Qur'an, thirty verses long, interceded for its companion until he was forgiven, and it is: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.﴾"

Abu al-Zubayr narrated from Jabir that the Prophet would not sleep until he had recited: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The revelation of the Book﴾ and ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.﴾ Tawus said: "These two surpass the rest of the surahs by seventy good deeds."

Abu al-Jawza' narrated from Ibn Abbas that a man pitched his tent over a grave while he did not realise it was a grave. He heard a reciter reciting ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾ until he finished the surah. He came to the Prophet and mentioned that to him, and he (ﷺ) said: "It is the one that saves, it is the one that prevents; it saves him from the punishment of the grave." Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi mentioned these reports in his Jami' with its chain of narration.

In other sources, al-Zuhri narrated from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman that the Prophet said: "The surah of al-Mulk will argue on behalf of its companion on the Day of Resurrection."

Murrah al-Hamdani narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that a man came to his grave from its sides, and a surah of the Qur'an turned away (the punishment) and argued on behalf of its companion until (it reached) Paradise.

Murrah said: "I and Khaythamah looked into it, and behold, it was the surah of al-Mulk, and Allah knows best."

His Exalted saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand﴾. We have explained that tabaraka is of the form tafa''ala, from al-barakah (blessing), and the meaning is that all blessings come from Him, the Exalted.

It is said: tabaraka means: He is magnified, sanctified and exalted. From it comes al-barak in the chest (the chest's expansion or tightness, as used in the sense of the heart's ease).

His saying ﴿in whose hand is the dominion﴾ means: the dominion of the heavens and the earth.

It is also said: the dominion of prophethood, by which He honours whoever follows it and humbles whoever opposes it. This is related from Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

His saying ﴿and He is Able over all things﴾ means: Capable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 2:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who created death and life﴾ — that is, death in this world and life in the Hereafter.

It is also said: "He created death" means the drop of semen in the womb, because it is dead, and "life" is that the spirit was breathed into it afterward.

It is also said: "He created death and life" means this world and the Hereafter.

Abu Salih related from Ibn 'Abbas that Allah Exalted created death in the form of a dusty-grey ram, which does not pass by anything, nor tread upon anything, nor does anything smell its scent without dying; and He created life in the form of a white-spotted female horse, which does not pass by anything, nor tread upon anything, nor does anything smell its scent without being given life.

He said: "It is less than a mule and more than a donkey; its stride is as far as the eye can see. Jibril was riding it on the day Pharaoh drowned, and from beneath its hoof al-Samiri took the handful."

Some of them said: He created this world for life and then for death, and He created the Hereafter for recompense and then for everlasting abiding.

And His saying: ﴿That He may test you, which of you is best in deed﴾ — that is, that He may try you, so that your good deeds and your evil deeds become manifest from you, and recompense you for them.

And His saying: ﴿best in deed﴾ — concerning it there are several opinions. The first: most complete in intellect and most scrupulous in abstaining from what Allah has forbidden; this is a transmitted saying.

The second opinion: "best in deed" means most sincere in deed.

The third opinion: "best in deed" means most ascetic toward this world and most willing to leave it; this is related from al-Hasan and Sufyan al-Thawri.

The fourth opinion: "best in deed" means the one among you who remembers death most and prepares for it best.

It is also said: the one among you with the greatest fear of Allah.

It is also said: the one among you most perceptive of the faults of his own self.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾ — we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who created seven heavens in layers﴾, meaning: some of them above others, and between every two heavens there is a command of His command and a creation of His creation.

And His saying ﴿You see no discrepancy in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: no flaw or defect.

It is also said: no disorder or inconsistency.

It has been read as "tafawut" (تفوت), and Abu 'Ubayd (Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam) preferred this reading.

Al-Farra' said: "tafawut" and "tafawat" have the same meaning, just as one says "ta'ahhada" and "ta'aahada" and other such forms.

It is also said: "tafawut" means that they do not cause one another to be lost, i.e., one part does not fail or contradict another.

His saying: ﴿Then return your gaze﴾, meaning: turn back the gaze.

His saying: ﴿Do you see any rifts?﴾, meaning: cracks, fissures and breaches.

It is also said: "fatara nab al-ba'ir" means the camel's tooth split open, i.e., cracked.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿Then return the gaze twice﴾ means: two times. Its meaning is: once after another, even if it exceeds two times, like a man who says to another: "I have said this to you time after time," when he has said it to him several times. Mentioned by al-Qaffal.

Some of them said: He only mentioned "two times" because a person, on the second look, becomes more perceptive, sees more, and looks more closely.

It is also said: The first look is with the eye, and the second with the heart.

Al-Farra' said: It is permissible that the meaning of "twice" (kartayn) is one time. They recited:

(Two deserts, two distant stretches, twice... I crossed it by its direction, not by two directions.)

And he meant one desert (mihmah).

And His saying: ﴿The gaze will return to you﴾ means: the gaze will return to you ﴿humbled﴾, meaning: subdued, ﴿and it will be weary﴾, meaning: exhausted, that is, weak in grasping what it sought of seeking a flaw or defect.

It is also said: a beast is "ḥasrā," meaning: exhausted.

The poet said:

(Upon it are the carcasses of the exhausted; as for their bones, they are white, and as for their hides, they are hard.)

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is that one exaggerates in looking, so the gaze returns to him humbled, having not attained what he wanted and not seen any defect or flaw.

And His saying: ﴿humbled﴾ (khāsi'an) derives from that, from their saying to a dog: "ukhsa'" (be gone and keep away). Al-Farazdaq said about Jarir:

(Be gone toward yourself, O Jarir, O abased one... We have reached the sky, its stars and its crescent.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps﴾, i.e., with lanterns (suraj). He named the stars "lamps" because of their giving light.

And His saying: ﴿and made them as missiles against the devils﴾, i.e., We pelted the devils with them to prevent them from eavesdropping (istiraq al-sam').

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Indeed, a star does not rise for the death of anyone, nor for his life, but it is an adornment of the world and missiles against the devils."

And on the authority of Qatadah, who said: "God created the stars for three things: He made them an adornment for the nearest heaven, missiles against the devils, and guidance for people in the paths. Whoever burdens himself with other than this has spoken without knowledge."

.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾, i.e., the kindled (al-mus'ara).

And on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: that al-Sa'ir is the fourth layer (tabaq) of Hell.

And His saying: ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Jahannam﴾. Jahannam was named Jahannam because of the depth of its bottom. The Arabs say: "a well (rikiyyah) jahannam," meaning: deep in its bottom.

And His saying: ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, meaning: the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 7:

His saying: ﴿When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring (shahiqan)﴾, meaning: from Jahannam. Al-shahiq is the first sound of the donkey.

It was also said: al-shahiq is the first part of its sound, and al-zafir is the last part of its sound.

It was also said: al-shahiq is in the chest, and al-zafir is in the throat.

It was also said: al-shahiq comes from the disbelievers when they enter Jahannam.

The first view is more apparent in this verse.

As for His saying: ﴿And it boils up (tafur)﴾, Ibn Mas'ud said: it seethes with a seething like that of a cooking pot with what is in it.

It is related from Mujahid: it seethes with the seething of abundant water over a little grain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿Almost bursting with fury﴾ means: it is kindled and splits apart.

It is said: "So-and-so is filled with rage, to the point that he almost bursts into flame" (yakad yatawaqqad).

And its fury is wrath against the enemies of Allah and its vengeance.

And His saying: ﴿Whenever a company is cast into it﴾ means: a people. ﴿Its keepers will ask them: Did there not come to you a warner?﴾ means: a messenger.

It is related from Mujahid that he said: "The messengers were from mankind, and the warners were from the jinn."

This is an abandoned (mahjur) opinion.

Their answer to the verse, "They will say, 'Yes, indeed. A warner came to us, but we denied him and said, Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'"

Al-Sam'ani: "*Kabir*" means "great."

It is also said that it means "sinners" (*khati'in*).

.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 10:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze."﴾ That is: we would have listened with the listening of one who discerns and reflects, and reasoned with the reasoning of one who ponders and considers. ﴿...we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ The meaning is: we did not hear the truth and did not understand it; that is, we did not benefit from our hearing and our reason.

Among some of the strange reports is that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "For everything there is a pillar, and the pillar of religion is reason."

It is also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A man may be among the people of jihad, the people of prayer and the people of fasting, and he may enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, but he will only be recompensed on the Day of Resurrection according to the measure of his reason." And this is a hadith with a good chain of narration (hasan al-isnad).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 11:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So they will admit their sin﴾, meaning: their sins. The singular is used in the sense of the plural. And His words: ﴿So away with the companions of the Blaze﴾, meaning: far away. It is said: "a place that is saḥīq," meaning: distant.

It is related from Mujahid: "Suḥq" is the name of a valley in Hell.

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, they will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾. That is: by the promise and the warning which are unseen (ghāba ʿanhu). It is also said: by Paradise and Hellfire. It is also said: in private, when alone.

.

As for His saying: ﴿they will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾, that is: a mighty (ʿaẓīm) one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 13:

His the Exalted's saying: ﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it openly﴾. In the tafsir (exegesis): the disbelievers, some of them would say to others, "Keep your speech secret so that the Lord of Muhammad does not hear it and inform him of your words." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: of what is in the breasts.

Al-Hasan said: He knows the secret just as He knows the open, and He knows the open just as He knows the secret.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 14:

The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ is an interrogative used in the sense of rebuke and reproach. The meaning is: Should not He who created the hearts know what is within the breasts?

It is also said: "Should not He know what He created?" Here "man" (من) is used in the sense of "ma" (ما), and it is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿By the heaven and He who built it﴾, meaning: and He who built it.

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾, meaning: the Subtle in His knowledge, who knows what appears and what is concealed and everything that is minute. It is said: "Subtle" (al-latif), and it is said: "the All-Aware" (al-khabir) is the Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 15:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He it is Who made the earth subservient to you﴾, meaning: made subdued (mudhallalah). Its subjugation (tadhlil) is the facilitation of walking upon it and of settling upon it.

And His saying: ﴿So walk in its shoulders﴾, meaning: in its sides. It is also said: in its paths (fijaj), and it is said: in its roads (turuq), and it is said: in its mountains (jibal).

It is narrated from Bashir ibn Ka'b al-Ansari that he used to recite this surah, and when he reached this verse, he said to a slave-girl of his: "If you know the meaning of His saying, ﴿in its shoulders﴾, then you are free." She said: "In its mountains."

The man was stingy with the slave-girl and began to ask Abu al-Darda', who said: "Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt; keep her."

Qatadah related from Abu al-Jald, who said: "The whole earth is twenty-four thousand farsakhs: twelve thousand for the Sudan (blacks), eight thousand for the Romans, three thousand for the Persians (ajam), and one thousand for the Arabs."

.

And His saying: ﴿And eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 16:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "That is, Allah."

And His statement: ﴿that He will not cause you to be swallowed up by the earth, and behold, it will shake?﴾ That is, it will convulse and turn. It is also said: "tamūru" means: He will cause you to be swallowed up by the earth until He places you in the lowest of the earths. The poet said:

(They shot, and so they struck the hearts, and you will not see blood flowing copiously except that it runs down the nostrils.)

That is: flowing.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven [that He will not] send against you a storm of stones?﴾ That is, "Do you feel secure from your Lord [that] He may send against you a hāṣib (a storm of pebbles), which He would use to destroy you." It is also said: "[a storm of] stones, by which He would destroy you."

Al-ḥaṣbā' (the pebbles) are stones.

And His saying: ﴿Then you will know how My warning was﴾ means: My admonition. The meaning is: I was truthful in my warning to you of the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And certainly those before them denied, so how was My disapproval?﴾ That is: My rejection (nakir, i.e., My denunciation and punishment).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them?﴾ It is said: "Saffa al-tair janahahu" (the bird spread its wing) when it spreads it out, and "qabadahu" (it folded it) when it strikes it [with the wings folded], and what is meant by "qabd" (folding) is the striking of the two wings against the two sides. This folding and spreading occurs in some birds, not in all birds, for some of them fold their wings in every state, and some of them spread them at times and fold them at others.

And His saying: ﴿None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: none holds them back from falling except the Most Merciful.

They said: The air is to the bird what water is to the swimmer; it swims in the air with its wings just as a person swims in water with his limbs.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing﴾, meaning: Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who is this that is an army for you to help you?﴾ Its meaning: Where is this one who is an army for you, to protect you from the punishment of Allah? It is an interrogative in the sense of rebuke and denial.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The disbelievers are only in delusion.﴾ That is: The disbelievers are only in delusion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 21:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Or who is it that can provide for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ The meaning is: Allah is the One who provides for you if He withholds His provision; so who is it that provides for you besides Him?

And His words: ﴿But they persist in arrogance and aversion.﴾ Ataww (arrogance) is persistence in disbelief, and nufur (aversion) is distancing oneself from the truth.

It is also said that the meaning is: obstinacy has led them to disbelief and to aversion from the truth, for the proofs are too clear and manifest to be hidden from anyone. The Arabs call every foolish, rebellious person who persists in falsehood ʿātin (arrogant transgressor).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 67, verse 22:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ (in the sense that) the one who walks prone on his face in misguidance does not see the truth.

It is also said: "prone on his face" means that he does not look ahead of him, nor to his right, nor to his left, nor behind him.

It is also said: this refers to the Hereafter, for Allah the Exalted will gather the disbelievers upon their faces, as the Qur'an states in another place. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the One who was able to make them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."

As for His words: ﴿Is one who walks upright on a straight path better guided?﴾, it means: one who walks on the path of truth with the light of guidance.

It is also said: he looks ahead of him, to his right, to his left, and behind him.

It is also said: this refers to the Hereafter.

It is related from ʿIkrimah that he said: the words ﴿Is one who walks prone on his face﴾ refer to Abu Jahl, and the words ﴿Or one who walks upright on a straight path﴾ refer to ʿAmmar ibn Yasir.

Some have related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it refers to Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, whose kunya was Abu ʿAmarah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: It is He who brought you into being and made for you hearing and sight and hearts; little thanks do you give.﴾ That is, say: little is your thanks for these blessings.
Almighty God's saying: (Say: He is the One who multiplied you on the earth). That is: He created you on the earth. ﴿And to Him you will be gathered.﴾ That is: in the Hereafter.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ That is, the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah).

The words of God Most High: ﴿Say, knowledge is only with God﴾, meaning: the knowledge of the Hour is with God.

And His words: ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾, meaning: a warner who makes the warning clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 27:

His saying: ﴿When they see it approaching﴾. Al-Mubarrad and Tha'lab said: that is, they see the punishment present before them.

It is also said: "near."

His saying: ﴿The faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed﴾. That is, evil and dejection will become evident in their faces.

It is also said: their faces will turn black.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said, "This is what you used to call for."﴾ In the irregular reading (shadh), "tad'un" was recited without shaddah (tashdid).

Some of them reported that "tad'un" and "tadda'un" have the same meaning. So His saying ﴿tad'un﴾ means: you used to call upon God by it.

His saying ﴿tadda'un﴾ means: you used to claim it against one another (tatadda'un), and this is like His saying, ﴿O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾. And He, exalted is He, said in another verse: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, hasten for us our share (qitt) [of punishment] before the Day of Account."﴾ That is, our portion of the punishment.

Ibn Qutaybah said: "tad'un" is an iftial (reflexive form) from supplication (du'a').

Some of them said: "tad'un" means: you used to deny (tukadhdhibun).

It is also said: you used to seek it hastily (tasta'jilun), and you used to doubt (timtarun) and dispute (takhtalifun).

It is also said: "tad'un" means: you used to wish for it (tamannun).

The Arabs say to someone else: "Ud'u ma shi'ta," that is: wish for whatever you want. This saying is close to the first saying.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 67, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if Allah destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us﴾. The people of tafsir said: The disbelievers used to say: "Muhammad and his companions are a morsel to be devoured; they will be destroyed soon." They were all hoping for falsehoods concerning the Messenger and his companions. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Have you considered: if Allah destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us﴾, meaning: whether we are saved or we are destroyed. ﴿Then who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?﴾ That is: then who will protect you from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He, when you have disbelieved in Him?

"The word of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say, "He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied. So you will know who it is that is in manifest error."﴾ That is: in clear error, and far removed from the truth and astray from it.

The word of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if your water should become sunken, then who will bring you flowing water?"﴾ That is: sunken (ghawran), and its meaning: gone away.

Qatadah said: "It is also said: the buckets cannot reach it." This was related by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

It has been said: the verse was revealed concerning the well of Zamzam and the well of Maymun, and both are in Makkah."

"And His saying: ﴿Then who will bring you clear water?﴾ Tha'lab said: That is, apparent (ẓāhir)."

"This is also reported from al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid and others."

"It is also said: [it means] sweet water, and it is said: [it means] flowing water."

"That is, Allah is the One able to bring it, and you cannot reach it by your own selves."
